newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Denmark wants greener and less secretive EU.
newsitem.headline: Denmark wants greener and less secretive EU.

text.p: Denmark, eager to improve the public image of the European Union, proposed on Tuesday new ways to boost the environment and to make the bloc's decision-making less secretive.
Copenhagen presented two separate proposals on amending the EU's treaty at the inter-governmental conference (IGC), which is negotiating reform of the 15-nation bloc and its institutions.
"What we at least would hope is to see a sort of change of culture in the EU in the direction of open government," said Niels Ersboell, Denmark's chief negotiator at the IGC.

Denmark wants the principle of public access to information held by EU institutions to be inserted in the EU treaty "in a way that ensures that the general rule is the right of access to information by the public."
In addition, it says the work of the Council of Ministers, the EU's main legislative body, should be made more open by introducing open debates at the first and final reading of legal proposals.
"This would to a large extent correspond to the practice of the national parliaments," the Danish proposal said.
Ersboell said there was "widespread acceptance" among other member states regarding access to documents but "widespread resistance" to the idea of open Council proceedings.
Denmark's Nordic neighbours Sweden and Finland earlier presented their own proposals on how to increase EU openness.
Ersboell said there were differences between the proposals.
"What is important is that it is clearly discernable that the Nordic countries agree on the general thrust in all these various areas, that is important," he said.

Denmark also wants it to be possible to introduce taxes to fight cross-border environmental problems with a qualified majority -- a proposal which looks set to encounter opposition as several countries are unwilling to give up taxation powers to a majority.
